title: slo-aware-trigger-generator-for-model-deployments
creator: Leah Chen
description: Design and implement a generative component (SLO Trigger Generator) that computes automated rollback conditions for model rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) using multi-signal SLOs: p95/p99 latency, error rate, token cost per request, and throughput. The component will produce actionable triggers (alerting + automated orchestration via rollout controller) with configurable sensitivity, hysteresis, and tenant-scoped baselines.
acceptance_criteria: Generator emits a json trigger payload consumed by rollout-controller with fields: metric, comparator, threshold, window, severity, cooldown
Can configure per-rollout policy: weightings for each SLO signal and minimum sample sizes
Automated rollback simulated in staging using historical traces with >=95% fidelity to expected rollouts
Integration tests that assert no false-positive rollback for small natural variance (95% false-positive reduction vs naive static-threshold)
Dashboard panel showing composite trigger score and contributing metrics for each canary
Rollout controller respects cooldown and cooldown suppression for infra-induced spikes
design_notes: We will compute a composite anomaly score = weighted_z(latency,p95) + weighted_z(error_rate) + weighted_z(token_cost) - weighted_z(throughput_effect) where weights are configurable per project
Baseline computed using sliding window of historical successful rollouts (7d default) with outlier removal (MAD) to avoid contamination
Thresholds tuned with a two-stage approach: (1) historical replay to pick initial weight and threshold, (2) conservative online ramping using a decaying learning rate
Use Welch's t-test for small-sample canaries to avoid misattributing variance; require min samples or fallback to traffic-based gates
Hysteresis implemented via dual thresholds: trigger_threshold and rollback_threshold with time_above_window to reduce flapping
Token cost SLO normalized per token and converted to z-scores using baseline mean/std; include model-specific cost multipliers
Throughput modeled as a stabilizing signal (increased throughput shouldn't by itself rollback), but we detect regressions where throughput drops while latency or error rises
Allow per-customer overrides: enterprise tenants can set stricter thresholds and override automatic rollback to notify only
Expose weight presets: conservative, balanced, aggressive. Default is balanced to prioritize availability over cost savings
Security: triggers are signals only; the rollout controller must check RBAC and billing policy before executing destructive actions
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created. Initial spike engineering design synced with PM and SRE. Decided to target canary controller integration first (canary flows) then A/B/shadow.
2026-03-03: Prototype scoring function implemented in feature branch eng/49577/trigger-gen-proto. Early results on 3 historical canaries show reduction in false rollbacks versus fixed 3-sigma rule.
2026-03-05: Review with SRE and Observability. SRE requested explicit cooldown and circuit-breaker semantics to avoid cascading rollbacks during infra incidents.
2026-03-06: Added min_sample_size tuning and Welch's t-test branch for low-traffic canaries. Created integration test plan and replay harness using data from runtime-1.22 canary traces.
2026-03-08: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/10234. Seeking design sign-off from PM and Security. Staging run scheduled 2026-03-10.
decisions: Decision 2026-03-03: Composite score approach accepted over isolated rules to reduce collision of simultaneous metric violations
Decision 2026-03-05: Implement dual-threshold hysteresis and a mandatory cooldown interval (default 10m) to prevent flapping
Decision 2026-03-06: Use historical replay for offline tuning and a conservative online ramp for weight updates (no immediate heavy changes in production)
Decision 2026-03-07: Rollback remains an action gated by rollout-controller; triggers are advisory by default for new customers until opt-in is confirmed
blockers: Observability sampling: current trace retention for canary-level metrics is 48h in some regions — need >=7d for baseline window. Ops ticket opened.
Per-tenant cost normalization requires billing rate API that is not available in private deployments — PM to scope enterprise-only feature flag
